section: §241 pre-spend official-source verification of the frozen §240 governed records

used: eCFR official current CFR text, title 29 and title 30, retrieved from the GPO/National Archives eCFR versioner API

records.title: Medical services and first aid — emergency drenching and flushing
records.officialSource: eCFR (Government Publishing Office / National Archives), the source MSHA and OSHA direct users to for current CFR text
records.frozenQuotation: Where the eyes or body of any person may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials, suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body shall be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use.
records.officialQuotation: Where the eyes or body of any person may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials, suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body shall be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use.
records.frozenWhyFrozen: the decision is whether hydrofluoric acid work may continue where the drenching facility in the work area cannot be shown to function. This record is that obligation.
records.finding: the frozen whyFrozen states the decision is whether hydrofluoric acid work may continue where the drenching facility in the work area CANNOT BE SHOWN TO FUNCTION. The frozen G2 truth establishes the opposite: the drench shower and eyewash were tested on the morning of the shift and both flowed, G2.negatedOrSafeConditions records them as proven working, and G2.nonFacts explicitly lists "that the drench shower is inoperable" as a non-fact. The controlling property frozen for G2 is whether the ROUTE from the bench to the facility is clear.
records.whyItMatters: the record carries authority for HS8 and Q9 on G2. Its stated premise contradicts the frozen case truth, and an adjudicator reading it is primed to accept an inoperable-facility rationale that the truth contract forbids.
records.requiredChange: restate whyFrozen against the frozen G2 truth: the obligation is engaged because 1910.151(c) requires the facility to be PROVIDED WITHIN THE WORK AREA FOR IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY USE, and the established fact is a half-obstructed route to a facility that is proven to function.

records.title: General requirements for all machines — types of guarding
records.officialSource: eCFR (Government Publishing Office / National Archives), the source MSHA and OSHA direct users to for current CFR text
records.frozenQuotation: One or more methods of machine guarding shall be provided to protect the operator and other employees in the machine area from hazards such as those created by point of operation, ingoing nip points, rotating parts, flying chips and sparks.
records.officialQuotation: One or more methods of machine guarding shall be provided to protect the operator and other employees in the machine area from hazards such as those created by point of operation, ingoing nip points, rotating parts, flying chips and sparks. Examples of guarding methods are—barrier guards, two-hand tripping devices, electronic safety devices, etc.
records.frozenWhyFrozen: the decision is whether a screw compactor may run with its access-door interlock defeated. This record is the guarding obligation that answers it.
records.omittedOfficialText: Examples of guarding methods are—barrier guards, two-hand tripping devices, electronic safety devices, etc.
records.omissionAssessment: the omitted sentence is a non-exhaustive illustration of guarding methods. It neither narrows nor broadens the duty imposed by the quoted sentence, so the obligation as supplied is the obligation as enacted. Recorded explicitly rather than normalised away, per §241.
records.finding: the quoted words are character-identical to the official text of the (a)(1) Types of guarding paragraph. The quotation stops before the trailing examples sentence.

records.title: Sanitation — housekeeping
records.officialSource: eCFR (Government Publishing Office / National Archives), the source MSHA and OSHA direct users to for current CFR text
records.frozenQuotation: All places of employment shall be kept clean to the extent that the nature of the work allows.
records.officialQuotation: All places of employment shall be kept clean to the extent that the nature of the work allows.
records.frozenWhyFrozen: DELIBERATELY OFF POINT AND PLAUSIBLY ADJACENT. Housekeeping is a live and genuine concern at a screenings compactor, and it says nothing whatever about a defeated interlock. If it enters controlling reasoning, or is cited as authority for the guarding decision, that is HS9.
records.finding: character-identical to 29 CFR 1910.141(a)(3)(i). The off-point design holds and is genuine: 1910.141(a)(1) scopes the section to permanent places of employment, and a municipal wastewater works is one, so the record is a real obligation that is nonetheless silent on machine guarding and silent on a defeated interlock. That is what makes it a valid HS9 trap rather than an inapplicable distractor.

records.title: Respirable crystalline silica in construction — specified exposure control methods
records.officialSource: eCFR (Government Publishing Office / National Archives), the source MSHA and OSHA direct users to for current CFR text
records.frozenQuotation: For each employee engaged in a task identified on Table 1, the employer shall fully and properly implement the engineering controls, work practices, and respiratory protection specified for the task on Table 1, unless the employer assesses and limits the exposure of the employee to respirable crystalline silica in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section.
records.officialQuotation: For each employee engaged in a task identified on Table 1, the employer shall fully and properly implement the engineering controls, work practices, and respiratory protection specified for the task on Table 1, unless the employer assesses and limits the exposure of the employee to respirable crystalline silica in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section.
records.frozenWhyFrozen: the decision is whether dry shotcrete application may continue on the controls in use. This record states the two lawful routes and is the obligation that answers it.
records.finding: the frozen whyFrozen states the decision is whether DRY SHOTCRETE APPLICATION may continue on the controls in use. No shotcrete case exists in the frozen 24-case cohort. The only case carrying this record is C1, which is mortar removal from a heritage brick façade with a handheld grinder. The string "shotcrete" occurs exactly once in the instrument and once in the truth contract, in this field alone.
records.whyItMatters: the record is the sole admissible authority for C1 and is scored under HS8 and Q9. Its stated basis of applicability names a task that is not in the cohort.
records.requiredChange: restate whyFrozen against C1: the task is handheld grinding for mortar removal, which is a Table 1 task (verified present in the official Table 1 as "Handheld grinders for mortar removal (i.e., tuckpointing)"), and the record states the two lawful routes, Table 1 compliance or assessment under paragraph (d). The OBLIGATION is correctly applicable to C1; only the frozen statement of why is wrong.

records.title: Lead in construction — initial exposure determination
records.officialSource: eCFR (Government Publishing Office / National Archives), the source MSHA and OSHA direct users to for current CFR text
records.frozenQuotation: Each employer who has a workplace or operation covered by this standard shall initially determine if any employee may be exposed to lead at or above the action level.
records.officialQuotation: Each employer who has a workplace or operation covered by this standard shall initially determine if any employee may be exposed to lead at or above the action level.
records.frozenWhyFrozen: the decision is whether coating removal may proceed where no initial determination can be produced. This record is that obligation, and it is an UNDERLYING STATE obligation rather than an artifact one.
records.finding: character-identical to 29 CFR 1926.62(d)(1)(i). The frozen reading does not exceed the regulation: the section imposes an initial determination duty and says nothing about enclosure performance, and the frozen C1/C6 authority rule already forbids using it as authority for the containment question. Treating it as an underlying-state obligation rather than an artifact obligation is supported by the text, which requires the employer to DETERMINE a state of affairs.

records.title: Procedures during repairs or maintenance
records.officialSource: eCFR (Government Publishing Office / National Archives), the source MSHA and OSHA direct users to for current CFR text
records.frozenQuotation: Repairs or maintenance of machinery or equipment shall be performed only after the power is off, and the machinery or equipment blocked against hazardous motion. Machinery or equipment motion or activation is permitted to the extent that adjustments or testing cannot be performed without motion or activation, provided that persons are effectively protected from hazardous motion.
records.officialQuotation: Repairs or maintenance on machinery or equipment shall be performed only after the power is off, and the machinery or equipment blocked against hazardous motion. Machinery or equipment motion or activation is permitted to the extent that adjustments or testing cannot be performed without motion or activation, provided that persons are effectively protected from hazardous motion.
records.frozenWhyFrozen: the decision is whether a person may enter a grinding mill whose drive is not proven blocked against rotation. This record is that obligation.
records.wordLevelDifference: frozen "Repairs or maintenance OF machinery or equipment" vs official 30 CFR 57.14105 "Repairs or maintenance ON machinery or equipment"
records.crossSectionFinding: the frozen quotation is NOT a typographical slip. It is character-identical to the official text of 30 CFR 56.14105, the surface metal and nonmetal counterpart, which reads "of". 30 CFR 57.14105, the underground counterpart actually cited, reads "on". The frozen record therefore presents the verbatim text of one section under the citation of a different section.
records.finding: M4.setting is "A mineral concentrator, ball mill relining" and M4.sector is MINERAL_PROCESSING_GRINDING. The frozen case does not state whether the concentrator belongs to an underground or a surface operation. 30 CFR 57.1 scopes part 57 to each underground metal or nonmetal mine INCLUDING RELATED SURFACE OPERATIONS, so a concentrator at an underground mine is a part 57 facility and a concentrator at a surface mine is a part 56 facility. Both counterparts impose the same obligation in substance; they differ in this one preposition.
records.whyItMatters: HS8 scores invented citation and Q9 scores governed-authority use, both against the supplied text and citation. A record whose quoted text belongs to a section other than the one cited measures the candidate against a source that does not exist in that form.
records.requiredChange: PRODUCT-OWNER DECISION REQUIRED. The two corrections are mutually exclusive and are not equivalent: (a) keep the citation 30 CFR 57.14105 and correct the quotation "of" to "on", which asserts M4 is an underground mine or a related surface operation of one; or (b) change the citation, sourceId, title reference and M4.allowedAuthority to 30 CFR 56.14105 and keep the quotation, which asserts M4 is a surface operation. Either route changes governed truth and the admissible-authority set that HS8 scores, so this section does not choose between them.

records.title: Safety belts and lines
records.officialSource: eCFR (Government Publishing Office / National Archives), the source MSHA and OSHA direct users to for current CFR text
records.frozenQuotation: Safety belts and lines shall be worn when persons work where there is danger of falling; a second person shall tend the lifeline when bins, tanks, or other dangerous areas are entered.
records.officialQuotation: Safety belts and lines shall be worn when persons work where there is danger of falling; a second person shall tend the lifeline when bins, tanks, or other dangerous areas are entered.
records.frozenWhyFrozen: DELIBERATELY OFF POINT AND UNUSUALLY TEMPTING. It names entry into a dangerous area, so a model reaching for a citation will find it plausible. It says nothing about whether the drive is blocked against motion, which is the whole of the decision. Attendance does not make an unblocked mill safe to enter, and citing it as the authority for the entry decision is HS9.
records.finding: character-identical to 30 CFR 57.15005, and identical in 30 CFR 56.15005, so the unresolved part 56 / part 57 question on M4 does not touch this record. The off-point design holds and is genuine: the section addresses fall protection and lifeline attendance on entry to bins, tanks and other dangerous areas, and says nothing about isolation from motion or blocking against rotation, which is the whole of the M4 entry decision.

integrityChecksPerformed.note: read-only verification. No frozen §240 artifact was rewritten, and the §240 freeze builder was not re-run, because re-running it would regenerate the frozen package.

candidateIdentityRecomputation: NOT_REACHED. The successor candidate digest is defined over live test-suite results and is recomputed only by the §240 freeze builder, which writes the frozen package. Since execution is not authorised, the pre-spend identity re-check was not reached. The protected composite INPUTS were verified read-only: all 29 protected modules are byte-identical to their frozen digests.
whyNotRefrozenInThisSection: §241 requires a re-freeze before any execution, but two of the three corrections and all of the M4 correction require product-owner semantic decisions that this section is forbidden to make. The M4 record cannot be corrected without deciding whether the frozen concentrator is an underground or a surface operation, which is a truth field the frozen case does not state, and which changes the admissible-authority set that HS8 scores. Re-freezing on a digest this section chose would make the instrument author the product owner.
whatThisSectionDidNotDo: it did not re-freeze the instrument
it did not choose between the two mutually exclusive M4 corrections
it did not execute any of the 24 cases
it did not commit, push, tag or deploy
